sections.overview: The runtime name is Hemigrammocharax multifasciatus, but Eschmeyer’s current catalogue treats Nannocharax multifasciatus as the valid combination. An Angolan survey also recorded it in the upper Okavango system.
sections.identification: It has dark vertical bars and a dark spot at the tail base.
sections.habitat: It favours vegetated river edges, oxbows and shallow lakes.
sections.diet: It takes small invertebrates and epiphyton from plants.
sections.behavior: It moves onto floodplains in the rainy season.
sections.reproduction: Breeding is reported in the southern African summer.
sections.ecology: Its range includes the Okavango and Zambezi basins.
sections.conservation: FishBase lists it as Least Concern, assessed on 1 May 2009, as Nannocharax multifasciatus.
